sections.h2: Who to call about property tax
sections.html:
The Trustee sends bills; the Assessor of Property answers questions about value. The Trustee is based at the courthouse in Athens, and the County Commission picks the rate.

  • Trustee: McMinn County Courthouse, 6 East Madison Avenue, Athens, TN 37303. Phone (423) 745-1291, fax (423) 744-1603.
  • Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:00, with extra Saturday mornings in February, 8:30 to noon.
  • Assessor of Property: appraises and classifies every parcel, checks sales, and takes reappraisal questions.

The Trustee's page describes three jobs for the office: collecting county property tax, keeping the county's accounts, and investing idle funds. The state tax relief program also runs through it. October mailings go to the January 1 owner, who is responsible for keeping the Assessor's mailing address up to date.

The county seat, Athens, is also the largest city. Etowah, Niota and Sweetwater are cities as well, with Calhoun, Englewood and Riceville rounding out the list. On July 1, 2025 the county had 57,404 residents, 7.8% more than in April 2020, and 24,424 housing units, of which 75.8% are lived in by their owners. Typical owner-occupied value is $211,800, typical rent is $803, and the median household earns $61,470. Builders pulled 125 permits in 2025.

School lines matter to buyers. McMinn County Schools runs most of the public schools, including McMinn County High and McMinn Central High. Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District cover grades K to 8 in their own areas, with the county high schools taking those students after eighth grade. Tennessee Wesleyan University is in Athens.

For the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026, the combined county rate is $1.0823 on each $100 of assessed value. Resolution 26-036, passed by the County Commission on June 15, 2026, set it, and the Trustee may round statements to a whole dollar. State classes drive assessment: farm and residential 25 percent, personal property 30 percent, industrial and commercial 40 percent, public utilities 55 percent.

Six funds share the levy, three of them school funds for McMinn, Athens and Etowah.

McMinn County levy by fund, per $100 of assessed value
FundLevy per $100 assessed
General Fund$0.4828
Other Capital Projects Fund$0.3871
McMinn School Fund$0.0944
Road and Bridge Fund$0.0829
Athens School Fund$0.0294
Etowah School Fund$0.0057
Total$1.0823

Cities can add their own tax to the county figure, so ask whether yours does. Rates are set each summer for the fiscal year beginning July 1, which means the number on a bill mailed in October reflects that June vote. If you are comparing years, remember that the assessed value, not the rate alone, drives the total.

Pay anytime from October 1 through the last day of February with no penalty. From March 1 the Trustee charges penalty and interest of 1.5 percent a month on what is unpaid.

You may mail payment; the postmark counts, and a receipt comes back the same way. A delinquent tax lien stays on the parcel through any change of owner, so buyers should run a title check. Old taxes must be paid before new ones, so a payment meant for this year first goes against any prior-year balance.

The office also opens on Saturday mornings in February. For payment methods beyond mail and in-person, call (423) 745-1291.

Talk to the Assessor of Property first, then go to the local equalization board. Under state law the county board hears a dispute before anyone else, and skipping it generally makes the value final. The Comptroller's appeals guide describes the board as five or more people who hear complaints and can change assessments.

  • County board: file by the date the Assessor gives you for this year's session.
  • State Board of Equalization: file by August 1 or on the 45th day after the county board mailed notice, whichever comes later.
  • Hearing: an administrative judge, who must put the decision in writing within 90 days.
  • Chancery court: petition within 60 days of the state board's final order.

One more rule for business owners: when a business fails to file a personal property schedule, the county forces an assessment, and only an appeal to the local board before that year's deadline can undo it. The schedule itself is due before March 1.

Homeowners should keep any appeal paperwork together: the Assessor's notice, your comparable sales, photos and the date you filed. If you miss a deadline, ask the Assessor or Trustee what options remain before assuming the value is final.

A state-funded program, run through the Trustee, helps elderly owners, disabled owners and disabled-veteran owners. Qualifying applicants have part of the home's tax paid by the State of Tennessee. File no later than 35 days after the February 28 payment deadline, which means early April. A veteran with a 100 percent rating may have other programs open. Bring proof of age, disability or rating, and income records when you apply, and ask the Trustee which documents it needs for your category before you go.

Income limits and credit amounts are set by the state each year, so call (423) 745-1291 for this year's figures before you apply. Relief repays part of a bill you have paid, so the bill itself still arrives.

sections.h2: Selling a McMinn County house with tax owed
sections.html:
A buyer's title search will turn up every unpaid year, because past-due tax stays attached to the house. It binds the property no matter who owns it, so a seller who is behind should expect the title company to insist on payoff at closing.

Before accepting an offer, get each year's amount from the Trustee, interest included. For an inherited house, one behind on payments or one needing repairs, the tax balance is simply another figure the title company takes from proceeds, and learning it early protects your closing date. Ask, too, whether a delinquent balance has accrued monthly interest since March 1, because the amount changes each month until paid.

A seller's to-do list: call (423) 745-1291 for the balance on each year, have the Assessor correct a wrong owner name or mailing address, pass the numbers to the title company, and look for the payoff on the settlement statement. Cash sales on short timelines follow the same list, just faster, and a clear payoff letter speeds them further. Do the calls early in the week, because the courthouse closes at four and the Saturday hours apply only in February, and write down the name of whoever gives you each figure.

faqs.q: What is the current McMinn County property tax rate?
faqs.a: $1.0823 per $100 of assessed value covers the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026, and the County Commission set it on June 15, 2026. Homes are assessed at 25 percent of appraised value.

faqs.q: When does McMinn County charge interest on late taxes?
faqs.a: From March 1 on, at 1.5 percent a month. You can pay penalty-free from October 1 until the last day of February.

faqs.q: Can I mail my McMinn County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The postmark date decides whether you were on time, and the Trustee mails back a receipt.

faqs.q: Which school systems affect a McMinn County tax bill?
faqs.a: Three funds on the levy support schools: McMinn, Athens and Etowah. Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District serve grades K to 8 in their areas, while McMinn County Schools covers most of the rest.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay old McMinn County taxes before this year's?
faqs.a: Yes, past-due taxes come first, and any such balance stays with the parcel whoever owns it.
